text.p: Headlines from major national newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
EL PAIS
- ETA gunned down a Spanish police inspector in Bilbao
- Catalan CiU approves soccer rights law, but calls it "interventionist" and "unconstitutional".
- Prime Minister Aznar considers EU Commission forecasts a backing of his policy
EL MUNDO
- Basque guerrilla group ETA kills a police inspector on the eve of the "Day of Struggle" called by its political arm HB
- Some kidnappers were executed by the army after they had surrended
CINCO DIAS
- For internet users: careful with the suppliers. There are 368 in Spain versus 150 in the U.S. and 13 in Germany
- Electrical, retail and motorway companies, absent from the stocks bullishness
- Schweppes versus Rebecasa, beverage firm of the Rato (Economy Ministry) family
- Brussels stops the trade of pigs in the Catalonia town of Lerida
EXPANSION
- Economy Ministry is discussing a 30 percent cut in company taxes
- Big banks boosted their business in investment funds, and cash in 174 billion pesetas in investment trusts fees
- Stocks market remains above 500 points
GACETA DE LOS NEGOCIOS
- The army will spend 400 billion pesetas to buy tanks
- Prime Minister Aznar rules out a 1997 mini-budget
- BP Oil Espana is preparing its entry in the gas battle
- BCH made 12.45 billion pesetas in the first quarter 1997, up 20.1 percent
-- Madrid Newsroom, + 341 585 8340
